explainBack.question: Why does signing SB 1168 not lower a California household's electricity bill this month?
explainBack.answer: Because the law's operative duty is that the CPUC 'assess opportunities' for rate structures inside a new or existing proceeding. Assessment is a study step: it identifies possible ways to make data centres pay their share of transmission, distribution, load and procurement costs. Only a later commission decision adopting an actual tariff would change how costs are divided among customer groups, and only then could a residential bill move.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: The operative verb and proceeding framing in P003–P004, and the explicit statement in P002 that neither law gives an immediate bill credit; source excerpts sb-opening and sb-operative-verb confirm 'shall assess opportunities'.
explainBack.assessment: The artifact fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language; the distinction between assessment duty and adopted rate is its central and best-executed move.

unseenTransfer.scenario: In 2027, a developer proposes a 25 MW data centre outside Fresno and applies for a conditional use permit. A neighbour wants to know what she can learn about the project now, whether she will ever see its individual electricity consumption published, and whether her PG&E bill will drop because of these laws. Her cousin's 8 MW server facility owner asks if he must report too.
unseenTransfer.question: What information becomes available to the neighbour, at which stage, and what determines any bill effect — and is the 8 MW facility covered?
unseenTransfer.answer: At permit stage the 25 MW facility is covered (≥10 MW) and must submit estimates to the local agency, so the planning record offers project facts she can read. After energization the owner reports to the state and at least annually, but the Energy Commission publishes only anonymized, aggregated data — she will never get a facility-level public dossier, and customer-specific consumption is protected from disclosure. Her bill depends not on this project's permit but on whether the CPUC's SB 1168 assessment leads to a proceeding that adopts a rate shifting costs to data centres. The 8 MW facility falls below the 10 MW definition and is excluded from AB 1577 reporting.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: P005 for permit-stage estimates and post-energization annual reporting, P006 for aggregate-only publication, P007 for the 10 MW threshold, exclusions and the proceeding-and-approved-rate test.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The scenario resolves entirely from mechanisms the article teaches, including the threshold edge case and the aggregate-publication limit — the transfer succeeds.

learningDisposition.rationale: One minor uncertain finding: 'energization' in P005 lacks a plain gloss at first use. A three-word parenthetical (e.g., 'when the facility is switched on') would repair it; everything else is clear or passing.

reader.summary: A disciplined, answer-first news brief that does its hardest job well: separating an enacted assessment-and-reporting process from an adopted rate or bill change, with scope honestly bounded to two of seven laws. Terms are glossed, limits sit beside claims, and the reader leaves with a specific verifiable test for future bill claims. Only quibble: 'energization' goes unglossed.

two-of-seven.reason: Chaptered-status excerpts show both bills approved September 21, 2026, and the Governor's announcement excerpt states seven data-centre bills were signed that day; P002 also discloses the two-of-seven scope limit.

sb-assess-opportunities.reason: The operative excerpt 'the commission shall assess opportunities for rate structures' plus the grid, load/procurement and residential-ratepayer subdivision excerpts match P003's three considerations closely and with correct attribution to the CPUC.

no-immediate-bill-result.reason: This is an absence claim resting on bounded inference: the operative verb is 'assess opportunities' within a proceeding and no adopted tariff or savings figure appears in any excerpt. The inference is sound and the article itself labels it as such, but the sources cannot affirmatively prove a negative.

ab-local-and-state-reporting.reason: Permit-stage submission to the local agency (ab-permit), post-energization reporting (ab-energization) and at-least-annual reporting (ab-annual) are directly supported. However, P005's specific estimate categories — 'energy, onsite-generation and sound' — are not visible in the supplied ab-permit excerpt, which truncates before the enumerated list, so that detail is unverified from provided evidence.

ab-publication-timing.reason: The ab-aggregate excerpt requires annual anonymized, aggregated publication on the commission website, and ab-2029 places the first data-centre load-trend assessment in the 2029 integrated energy policy report — both matching P006 verbatim in substance.

ab-threshold-exclusions-privacy.reason: The 10 MW definitional floor (ab-threshold), the named public-research, public-safety, national-security, publicly owned and utility exclusions (ab-exclusions), and the bar on disclosing customer-specific data (ab-privacy) all directly support P006–P007, and the article does not overextend these limits to the other five laws.

factualIntegrity.reason: All material claims trace to chaptered statutory excerpts or the official announcement with correct attribution; the two qualified claims are a properly labelled bounded inference and one estimate-category detail truncated out of the supplied excerpt, neither a misstatement.

freshnessReviewability.reason: Signing date (September 21), access/check date (September 26), lastCheckedAt timestamp and named primary sources make every time-sensitive claim checkable.

datedChange.reason: The artifact cleanly distinguishes the September 21 enactment from future events: the pending CPUC proceeding, post-energization reporting and the 2029 report milestone.

consequenceAndUncertainty.reason: Consequences are concrete (10 MW threshold, aggregate publication, local planning records) while uncertainty survives explicitly — no tariff selected, no household saving calculated, no facility-level dossier promised.

learningDisposition.rationale: The specific 'energy, onsite-generation and sound' estimate categories in P005 cannot be verified because the supplied ab-permit excerpt cuts off before the statute's enumerated list; supplying that list would resolve the only open item. No misstatement was found.

Dates, attribution and limits are handled carefully throughout.
